reviews.comment: Very Reachable professor, great lectures and easy home works. I dont know why others are rating him low, But the lectures were really amaizing. But there are some downsides, I would like really point out. All of my learning from this class was from external sources. MEEN-260 is already a confused and jumbled class, and he did not make it better.
By far the worst professor I have ever had. Whatever you do, please take another class or do not bother to take his class. He will make you question why you are paying tuition to attend his class.

Okay, I've reviewed Haglund before for 225, but taking 260 with him was a whole new world. His tests were so much easier than I expected after suffering through statics. There's a lot of writing, and the graders are really tough, but go to class and study for the two exams, and you'll be totally fine.

I got an A because my exam grades made up for my lackluster lab grades. Do well on the exams and lab memo and you're set. 260 is just a difficult class that takes a ton of time, don't conflate that with Dr. Haglund himself. He was kind and responsive to me even though I didn't make it to a single lecture on time (8 am section).

okay meen 225 is an insane class already workload wise, but he doesnt make it any better. he went out of his way to make this honors section significantly harder than any honors class ive taken, but not entirely his fault. he is a very good person but not a good prof for 225. when you ask a question he says 'use your best engineering judgement'.

Took his course against multiple warnings. He completely re-arranged the course content to fit his schedule and to his likings so you are not syncd with other sections. FAMOUS FOR: "an exam is a test of your knowledge, you are not expected to get everything right so nobody should expect even high 90s on exams" - take this as a warning..;
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WHY AM I PAYING TENS OF THOUSANDS IN TUITION TO HAVE TO TEACH MYSELF EVERYTHING BECAUSE THE PROFESSOR SOLVES ONE PROBLEM PER CLASS

He does not care about his job, and it is evident in the way he lectures. His rubrics are unclear and harsh. He does not make himself super available. When asked for help, he ALWAYS responds with 'use your judgement'.

John Haglund is an abysmal professor.  He takes an hour to solve one statics problem and rambles in a monotone voice, leaving me longing for the end of class and wishing for better days.  His tests are graded under a microscope and you can easily get points off even if your answer is right.  The projects take over 10 hours and are overcomplicated.

He is objectively not a good professor. There is well over 10+ hours of homework every single week, and his tests are much harder than other classes. His lectures are working through a single problem, and then the homework is due THAT NIGHT with well over 20 questions. DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN, YOU WILL STRUGGLE.

Took 315 over the summer semester. Haglund did a great job of explaining material in pragmatic ways and applying the theoretical knowledge to real life examples. It's a difficult class, but he grades fairly and gives partial credit on exams.
MEEN 260 is just a mess. Lots of time is required for this class (mostly for the labs).

Dr. Haglund is very good at explaining concepts at a high level, but rarely does examples. He does post resources where the a problem similar to homework is solved step-by-step though. Attending lectures is a must because of how much content there is for Thermo. Not as bad of a class as I was expecting though. Homework also takes like 8hrs to do
One of the best teachers I've had so far at TAMU.

This class was curved into oblivion or else I would have gotten a 30. I couldn't figure this guy out. By the end I had an alright understanding of thermo. You absolutely need to reed the book cause otherwise homeworks are impossible to finish. Unfortunately I didnt realize this till the very end. Very conceptual lectures.

Dr. Haglund really cares about his students and really makes an effort to be accessible for office hours, hwk help, clarification, etc. Thermo is a tough course, but Dr. Haglund gives you a great understanding of how to approach and solve problems. Though his tests are difficult, he does curve heavily, and you will learn a lot having taken him.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thermodynamics is a tough course no matter who the professor is, but Dr. Haglund does what he can with what he is given. He has office hours nearly every day and they are the non-negotiable key to making the class and homeworks tolerable. He is very kind and witty; he evidently cares about the subject and the students alike.

260 is just a bunch of different topics mashed into 1 class. Haglund cannot change the fact but truly cares about students' learning and is very kind and helpful in office hours. Hws are challenging but going to office hours will help a LOT. He also gives a lot of in-class extra credit so don't skip. I would def take him again.

Haglund's hw is challenging only because it tests your problem-solving. Tests are easier than hw. He is extremely helpful in office hours. If you genuinely put in effort you will do well. Always uplifts students and is great at answering emails. He gives a lot of extra credit so don't skip. Get ready to spend hours on hw, but it is doable.

260 is a very heavy class no matter what prof you have.. thats why I think that he is rated so low. He is enthusiastic about this class and always goes back and reviews concepts before beginning lecture. I would recommend making different sections in your notes for "writing' "ethics" and 'technical' because each lecture is one of those.

Took him for 315. My biggest gripe is he is really unlikely to be direct when asking questions when sometimes a simple straightforward answer is all that's needed to finish a HW. Overall though I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures and found myself enjoying the class at the end. HW sometimes require asking him directly but nothing absurd. Good prof.

I have had Professor Haglund for 4 classes at A&M. He is extremely kind, always accessible for help, passionate and wants you to succeed. 
However, he is a self described thermofluids geek - so avoid his classes outside of that. Grades typically get curved, and if you try you can achieve an A.

The lecture is absolutely useless when it comes to solving homework problems. Dude writes his own homeworks so they cannot be found anywhere and you are just left with scavenging the internet for clues for hours only for him to give you a 65 on the homework which is meant to be a learning tool. Homework is 20% of total grade btw

Professor Haglund has a unique teaching style that I never really got into. I would go to all lectures, but just be very confused every time. I recommend just redoing homeworks and in class assignments to help prepare for exams. I will say that homework and exams are graded fairly and generously. I barely made an A in this class bc of it (90.1)
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know whether it's because Dr. Haglund isn't a good teach or if MEEN 260 is just a poorly designed course, but the course was very hard. The class lacks any real focus and switches between topics at the drop of a hat. No one I talked to ever felt like they were prepared for an exam.

lectures very underprepare you for homework and tests, be ready to spend many hours doing a couple problems if you want to complete them. the class is pretty bad overall and needs a lot of work and unfortunately this has been known for years but laziness has persisted and the class quality is still very poor. lab instructions worst documents ever
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: reviews for this guy so accurate. does not prepare you for any of the homeworks, grades extremely hard. Has a bad ego he makes own homework so even having the whole internet the homework will consume so much time UNNECESSARILY. very very very poor quality homeworks. Watch out cause the meen 315 class he teaches is the same form of bad
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Partly Dr. Haglund's fault partly the graders' fault. It took them a month and a half to grade the exams and you will not have any idea how you are doing in the class since the homeworks took over 2 months to get graded as well. No curve at all, but the labs and lab assignments are fairly easy. Sadly, other profs suck too, just a poorly run course.

The class was structured so that the homework material was not taught until after the assignment was due, but the materials needed to learn the material on your own were not provided. This meant that it was incredibly difficult to complete these assignments in any reasonable amount of time.

Honestly, I'm not really sure why Haglund has gotten such bad reviews for 315 online. I've thoroughly enjoyed this course. He makes it interesting and challenges his students without being unfair. As long as you attend every lecture and genuinely learn/understand every homework, you should do fine. Homeworks are extremely similar to exams FYI

Dr. Haglund really cares for his students and is passionate about what he teaches. Unfortunately, MEEN 260 is pretty dull and the lectures are tough to follow. There is also a lot of homework in this class so stay ahead. Definitely practice the problems in the textbook to prepare for the exams.

Dr. Haglund is a great lecturer but the concepts of the class are often dull. He does not post his personal lecture notes that he uses in class, so it makes it difficult to perform some problems on the hw and exam. Overall the class is not as hard as previous years but the amount of work is still exhausting. This is not all his fault though.

This man. THIS MAN.
He is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. If you can avoid him like the plague. He does not stay on topic in class and half the time the material in lab is not even discussed until after the lab. I just took my final and half of my grades still are not in. GFL if you get stuck with him, you will need it.

A very passionate professor about the subject. Gives helpful examples to understand key concepts for thermo-fluids. Also, he curves very generously. Put in the work and you will not be let down with the results. Only downside is the group projects take up a lot of time and effort, which will not help if your group is incompetent.

This class was very difficult itself. Its an advanced course of thermodynamic. The project was fully coding and it was very difficult without someone knowing coding really well. He cares for his students but he is just too smart to really understand the struggles of the students. He answers questions very well but his material was just hard

His Thermo-fluids classes are a night and day difference from other courses he teaches. He cuts to the chase, answers questions well, and is accommodating to those with an internship. So long as you do your work and try your best to understand the material (because it is not easy), it is very rewarding.

Dr. Haglund was amazing for summer HT. Never failed to give extra credit. Ask questions, look at the textbook, and thoroughly do your work. He was very accommodating for those who had an internship like me and it did not take much of my time to do the work. He also curved exams generously and you always knew where your letter grade stood.

Generally very personable, but class lectures did not prepare me for homework or exams. The class itself was also poorly structured, with 5 profs teaching 5 different things 5 different ways, and on both exams I ran into problems I had no idea how to work. Grades on the first exam took 5 weeks before they were posted.

Provides basic notes and never solves problems in lecture. Assignments take eternities to complete because you have to teach yourself the material. All assignments are graded for accuracy so if you miss one step you are sol. Gives take home exams but are near impossible. No source will help, not even textbooks. Don't take him.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. too many assignments(45 total!) 4 long individual projects, 4 quizzes, midterm, and a final. He is sooo boring, making his lectures impossible to listen too. Even with the huge number of assignments, no late credit is accepted. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is very detailed about the course. The hw for all meen 225 section is very long so Chegg is the goal to have. He is a good prof to have. Stat/Dynamic isn't an easy class to take.
This mans purpose in life is to torment his student's with useless and difficult busy work and gives terrible grades

Loads of homework. You just go through the motions rather than learn the material well. It's a shame A&M thinks quantity>quality in this curriculum. Professor Haglund isn't bad. Lectures are ok, but often don't cover the more complex problems you'll have to figure out later. He's very helpful in office hours if you show you want to learn.
reviews.ratingTags: So many papers--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not sign up for Haglund unless you wanna teach yourself the course, and be graded very harshly on every homework/project (of which there are many). Poor excuse for a professor who does everything in his power to make the class harder.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This is the only time i've did a ratemyprof but i've had Haglund for MEEN 421 and MEEN 344. I like the class because the way he teaches- you are forced to learn the material and you really feel respected under his instruction. HW's and tests are hard but he curves most people to A/B so don't worry about grade. He creates a good learning atmosphere
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever taken at Texas A&M. He is rude and dont even bother going to office hours because he doenst answer questions and talking to him is a waste of time. I hated 260 but the class was even worse when I had John as a professor. I just found out I had him this semester and I immediatly switched out of it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: MEEN 225 is a very hard class. And Haglund makes it even harder would be an understatement. The workload is more than any class I've ever taken. Homeworks are given without giving a second thought about the time each one takes. Projects are pointless and a nightmare. In general, the worst experience I've ever had.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is very tough. Every week, there is over 10 hours of online homework, and either a take home test or a project (usually over 20 hours of work). Spent more work on this class than all my other classes combined. Haglund's lectures are okay but I was usually getting lost since he goes so fast and expects everyone to already understand it.

This subject is death in itself. Haglund doesn't really try to help you though. Any time you ask him a question, he just responds with "use your engineering judgement". It pissed me off to no end. Lectures never helped me, and the projects were unnecessarily difficult. Hardest class I've taken, and I could have used more guidance.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class made me cry a lot. not always haglunds fault as projects and homework are pretty standard among all the sections but man does he make it worse. his lectures were more theoretical than actually learnign to do problems we would spend an entire 50 mins doing a single problem that should take 10 he just makes everything harder than it is

Haglund gets a lot of undeserved criticism in my opinion. I had him for MEEN225 and really enjoyed his lecturing and felt like he cared about my learning. The class itself is a lot of work, but not by his design. His passion for mechanics is clear and contagious. Sometimes the way he answers questions can be frustrating, but you get used to it!

Haglund is not bad when it comes to explaining the material and definitely knows what he is talking about. However, he is not helpful at all when posed with a question and will more often than not tell you to use your "engineering judgment". The workload was insane but that is not Haggy's fault. Overall below average professor

If you want to spend entire weekends on homework and then have a task of a project that should reasonably take a few weeks to do assigned the week before finals then take John Haglund. If you want to save your sanity and still get the same credit with much less work, take literally anyone else.

Haglund is the best lecturer I've had at A&M so far. He is a fantastic teacher and gave me a better understanding of the material. One downside is that he assigns a TON of homework, but you get used to it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Unless you are a genius and have an incredible talent for soft mechanics, don't take a single one of his classes. The time spent on homework is ridiculous, averaging 10+ hours for each question (there are several). His exams are way too extensive for the 50 min allowed, you won't finish. Just do yourself a favor and don't.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: i really dont like this man
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Homework took 8++++ group hours of work. Completing it robs you of any study time for the tests. The homework is not like the tests. The lectures are conceptual with no examples and I still failed the conceptual test questions. Detailed written examples/work out problems are posted but it was a poor replacement for the professor going through it
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His lectures are interesting conceptually, but are 0 help when it comes to the homework or exams. This class is effectively self taught with no chance of partial credit on any test question, making the course much much harder than it needs to be.

I believe he spends most of his time trying to be very literal and specific. He talks more than he teaches, emphasizes easy concepts, and doesn't focus on concepts that should be discussed heavily in class. If he spends more time doing examples than just explaining random easy concepts, everyone would get A's. He overcomplicates everything!
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He talks about the "philosophy" of teaching, instead of actually getting to the point of the subject matter. He loses his students by telling them stories about signal analysis and how to "philosophically" theorize signals, instead of logically breaking it down and teaching the basics. Ineffective considering the high amount of work given.

Not many in class examples were done. He over-complicates the material. In this course (not just with this prof) be prepared to teach yourself the material. It would help to have some friends in other professors classes. Go to class for the quizzes, do the homework and study with friends and you should do alright.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very enjoyable lectures, Haglund is possibly my favorite lecturer at A&M thus far. Very NOT-enjoyable homework. His style is to make YOU (not chegg) work for understanding, and to do that he makes you struggle. I like this, but can see why students get upset about it since it is time consuming and stressful. However, his grading and tests are fair.

Haglund made the comment in class "if you come to me during office hours and you tell me that you don't know how to approach a problem, or you are confused, I will say 'good.'" This man is incredibly unhelpful and I have learned next to nothing in his class.

Assignments were graded very harshly . While answers may have been correct, if it was not accurate to the third significant figure, the answer was considered wrong and no credit would be awarded for the entire question, regardless of multiple parts. Posted example problems helped for exams but tests were difficult with little partial credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: It is sometimes difficult to get an answer from Prof. Haglund.

Had him for MEEN 225. Subject itself was hard and he gave a ton (several tons actually) of homework. He is a pretty decent lecturer, but you HAVE to spend lots (more than any class I've had) of outside class time studying and doing the math or you will fail. Mostly online homework through Pearson plus bi-weekly "projects" aka long irl engr problems
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is the most inconsiderate professor that you can have, the material is the same as the other classes but somehow he manages to complicate the content. He doesn't teach, he doesn't go over examples, and he doesn't care about anyone but himself. Impossible to ask questions because he tries to reply in a smart ass response. OR ELSEPAY CONSEQUENCES
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Haglund did his best to make the boring material of Mech Measurements and make it somewhat interesting. He was engaging, most respectful prof I've ever had, NEVER made a student feel dumb, and though his tests were quite difficult, he curved the class a little bit to compensate. Office hours with him will make everything make sense. Great professor

Doesn't post much online in the way of lecture notes. I had to wait until the day before the final to get almost all lab grades back. The homework is very difficult. If 1/2 credit wasn't given for completion/formatting, I may not have survived the class. Tests are HARD, and the end-of-semester group lab project is a nightmare! Do NOT take his class
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Haglund is known to be a hilarious teacher.  What people don't tell you before taking him is he doesn't teach.  He tells stories about his life, gives you a few definitions, and then expects you to know how to solve problems.  I need examples to learn in engineering classes, but he doesn't give you any help to learn. But sure, the man is funny.

This professor is incredibly detail oriented, so be sure to read the instructions very thoroughly before turning the homework and labs in. A lot of self-teaching was necessary as well in order to understand some of the concepts as they were not explained thoroughly in lecture and there were no power-point slides. Heavy homework load, and no grace.
This class is a lot of work. Professor Haglund will take 45 min to explain one problem, so there is not very much practice which is not good when it comes time for tests (which there are a LOT of).
Very heavy on the homeworks, but he teaches the material well.  He is also helpful if you have other questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Good lecturer and very clear to understand. Do not skip class because he won't let you see the notes in office hours. Tests are relatively easy if you study everything goes over in class and you work a lot of examples. The biggest con is that he writes his own homework so it can be extremely difficult to get correct answers on new material.

Haglund is awesome, one of the best profs in MEEN. I took him for MEEN 315, 260, and 363. He is probably the best lecturer I've had, I learn so much from him, and he has tons of office hours. With that said though, some students can be frustrated by his tough HW and few examples solved in class. It is a little frustrating, but he is the best.

Haglund taught this class very well.  Completely different teaching style than that of MEEN 260.  I took MEEN 363 as a summer course, we had one homework assignment each week and 6 exams.  Haglund did a great job explaining application, as well as delving into each type of problem with a lot of thought and a desire to teach the class.

A textbook wasn't required for this course, which made it very tough.  For me, working many examples on my own time helps prepare me for exams and I was unable to do so.  The only form of practice was from the homework, which he made up on his own, therefore, no examples could be found on the internet in order to help.
Dr. Haglund is a nice guy that does actually want you to learn. He gives plenty of theory and plenty of examples. Lots of homework, but it helps with preparing for exams.
